issues.description: default_raise() sentinel pattern is stale; its contract was tied to <3.10 limitations now removed
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py still carries `default_raise` with the comment 'This should be impossible to hit and is just for < 3.10 compatibility' and uses it as `default_factory=default_raise` on many fields. With kw_only=True now uniformly applied, the correct contract is 'required keyword argument' — expressible by simply omitting a default. Keeping `default_raise` weakens the type's invariant (a field appears to have a default-producing factory but in fact raises), which is exactly the kind of leaky postcondition LSP asks us to forbid. Replace with no-default kw-only fields and delete the sentinel, or rename and document it as 'required-field marker' if retained for streamable's machinery.
issues.lines: around the default_raise definition and all field(default_factory=default_raise) sites

issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 globally ignored — defers the very contract modernization this PR motivates
issues.detail: The PR description states Union/Optional should become `A | B`/`A | None`, but ruff.toml adds `UP045`, `UP007`, `UP035` to the global ignore list with a TODO. This freezes the codebase in a mixed type-syntax state where the contract (what the modern type expression is) is left ambiguous across modules. For a long-lived multi-team codebase, the right move is either (a) land the sweep in this PR, or (b) file a tracked issue referenced from the TODO with an owner and a kill date. As written it is SPEC-MISSING at the lint-policy boundary.

issues.description: Dead comment about 3.9 coverage quirk remains after the workaround was removed
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/conditions.py the `continue` line was de-annotated but the surrounding code still reflects defensive structure that existed to satisfy 3.9 coverage. Worth a quick audit that no other `# pragma: no cover` comments survive whose only justification was 3.9 behavior — they now misrepresent the contract of what is and isn't tested.

issues.description: kw_only_dataclass helper removed but call sites duplicate the same decorator literal
issues.detail: Every former `@kw_only_dataclass` site now repeats `@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)`. The abstraction was real (it encoded the project-wide convention 'streamable request types are frozen kw-only dataclasses'). Inlining loses that named contract; if the convention is intentional and load-bearing, restore a thin helper (without the version branch) so future readers see the intent rather than a repeated literal. This is the classic 'abstraction hides intent, not just implementation' question.
issues.lines: all @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) decorators on streamable request classes

issues.description: Install.sh and Install.ps1 minimum-version check is inconsistent with the stated contract
issues.detail: install.sh still tests `PYTHON_MINOR_VER -lt 7` while the user-facing error says '>= 3.10'. The check should be `-lt 10` to match the new contract; otherwise the precondition advertised to the caller (Python 3.10+) is stronger than the precondition actually enforced (3.7+), which is a small but real contract drift between docs and code.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml: `dnf search python3.12` left in CI step
issues.detail: The Amazon/Rocky prep steps run `dnf search python3.12` before installing — a diagnostic that produces noise and, more importantly, has no contract: it neither asserts the package exists nor fails the step. Either drop it or replace with `dnf list --available python3.12` gated by `set -e` so the precondition (python3.12 is installable) is actually checked rather than merely searched.
issues.lines: Amazon Linux and Rocky prep blocks

review.summary: From an abstract-data-type and contract perspective, this PR is mostly a clean simplification: removing version-conditional dataclass construction restores a single substitutable contract for command and request types (kw-only frozen dataclasses), which is exactly the kind of invariant collapse LSP discipline rewards. The chief remaining concerns are residual scaffolding whose contract was tied to the removed 3.9 branch — `default_raise` as default_factory, the `kw_only_dataclass` helper inlined into a repeated literal, and stale coverage pragmas — plus a lint-policy gap (UP007/UP035/UP045 globally ignored with no owner or deadline) that leaves the Union/Optional modernization promised in the description unspecified. Install scripts also drift slightly from the new precondition (>=3.10) while internally still checking >=3.7. None of this is a substitutability violation, but several items are SPEC-MISSING that the next maintainer will pay for. The architectural direction is correct; the cleanup is half-done.
